facts.text: Operator behavior change is the way people start to work differently once a protective system exists, including risk compensation (taking more risk because they feel protected) and over-reliance (letting the system do the watching).
facts.quote: Operator behavior change is the way people start to work differently once a protective system exists, including risk compensation (taking more risk because they feel protected) and over-reliance (letting the system do the watching).

facts.text: A protective system that is wrong too often can be distrusted and disabled by operators.
facts.quote: a system that is wrong too often is distrusted and disabled.

facts.text: The booklet names calibrated trust—trusting the protective system exactly as much as it deserves—as the goal for operator behavior.
facts.quote: The goal the booklet names is calibrated trust, trusting the system exactly as much as it deserves [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Off-road evidence of operator behavior change is qualitative only.
facts.quote: Off-road, the evidence is qualitative only.

facts.text: Underground workers changed where they stood, removed tags and asked for bypasses in response to protective systems.
facts.quote: Underground workers changed where they stood, removed tags and asked for bypasses

facts.text: Regulators worry about a "silver bullet" mindset toward off-road protective systems.
facts.quote: regulators worry about a "silver bullet" mindset

facts.text: An MSHA commenter said miners had taken higher risks because of a false sense of security.
facts.quote: an MSHA commenter said miners "have taken higher risks because of a false sense of security" [Chapter 4].

facts.text: The booklet rates the evidence for off-road workers learning protective-system zones and changing close-proximity tasks as moderate.
facts.quote: learning the zones and changing close-proximity tasks (moderate evidence)

facts.text: The booklet rates the evidence that off-road protective systems are overridden or disabled as strong, but the frequency is unknown.
facts.quote: overriding or disabling (strong that it occurs, frequency unknown)

facts.text: Over-reliance on off-road protective systems is reported but not quantified.
The booklet found no surface-mining data showing operators driving faster or following closer because the machine will brake.
facts.quote: driving faster or following closer because the machine will brake (not found in surface-mining data) [Chapter 4].

facts.text: On-road drivers who trusted other vehicles' automatic braking braked later themselves; the booklet identifies a possible parallel for ground crew who assume a machine will stop for them.
facts.quote: On the road, drivers who trusted other vehicles' automatic braking braked later themselves, a possible parallel for ground crew who assume a machine will stop for them [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Operator behavior change cannot be seen in a four-month window or in a simulator and needs months of field time.
facts.quote: Behavior change cannot be seen in a four-month window or in a simulator; it needs months of field time

facts.text: The booklet lists evaluation of operator behavior change as uncompressible and assigns it to staged release with field monitoring.
facts.quote: the booklet lists it as uncompressible and assigns it to staged release with field monitoring [Chapter 1].

facts.text: Missing quantitative data on operator behavior change should be collected during pilot deployment rather than assumed.
facts.quote: The missing numbers should be collected during pilot deployment rather than assumed [Chapter 4].
